audit.why: 51.55% over 291 games, and the late section says so out loud — 'that's the honest read on a 51.55% lane that's barely yours on paper'. Camille takes levels 1-5 and the item stages, Zac reclaims the game at two items. That matches the already-audited mirror at audits/top/zac__camille.json, which puts levels 3-6 in Camille's column from Zac's side.

The blob economy is correctly identified as the spike mechanism rather than raw levels — Camille's window is when her Tactical Sweep heal outpaces his blob pickups, and it closes at two items. Elastic Slingshot is 21s at rank 1 falling to 9s, which is worth naming since the whole 'hold E to dodge it' plan depends on how often it comes back.

audit.whatIsWrong: Camille's R is described twice as dragging Zac somewhere — 'R drags him into the arena away from his team' (spikes[1].text) and 'pull him into the arena away from his team and his loose blobs' (mid). It does neither. Zac's E is called 'Slingshot' rather than Elastic Slingshot, his passive is only 'his passive' and his ultimate is never named.
audit.why: Riot's text for The Hextech Ultimatum: 'Camille dashes to target champion, anchoring them to the area.' She travels to Zac and traps him where he already stands — nothing is displaced and he is not separated from his team or his blobs. The mirror states this correctly from his side ('her R does not move you — she comes to you'), so the two pages currently contradict each other, and the advice here is inverted in the way that costs games: a Camille who ults expecting to extract Zac from his team has instead put herself inside it. Riot's names are Cell Division (P), Stretching Strikes (Q), Unstable Matter (W), Elastic Slingshot (E) and Let's Bounce! (R).
audit.corrected: The R restated as an anchor that brings Camille to him, matching the mirror; Elastic Slingshot, Cell Division and Let's Bounce! named.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Keep E held to dodge his Q pull and Slingshot, then re-stun once they're on cooldown' names two cooldowns and gives neither.
audit.why: Stretching Strikes is 14s at rank 1 down to 8s and Elastic Slingshot is 21s down to 9s, against Hookshot's 16s. At rank 1 his engage is the longer of the two, so holding E to bait it is a winning trade early — and by rank 5 both of his are shorter than hers, which is the mechanical reason the plan expires exactly when the text says the lane does.
audit.corrected: Both numbers written into wants.you[2] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Stretching Strikes is described only as a pull, and Cell Division's revive is described with no timer — 'his passive revives him from a surviving blob'.
audit.why: Riot flags Stretching Strikes as an auto-attack reset as well as a pull, so the wind-up is the tell for his opener rather than the cast — _missing-interactions.json flags exactly this for the pairing. And the mirror establishes that the Cell Division revive runs on its own five-minute cooldown, which turns 'unkillable' into a state with an expiry: a Zac who has already revived is a normal tank for the next five minutes, and that is when to take the fight.
audit.corrected: The auto-reset tell written into whys[1]; the revive's five-minute window written into late.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are a clean skill phase — you both want short trades, but the goo blobs he drops on ability use let him heal back anything you poke, so don't burn HP unless you can step on the blobs afterward to deny the pickup. Start W for the outer-edge max-HP damage and self-heal, and respect that his Q (Stretching Strikes) pulls you in and his W (Unstable Matter) nukes you for flat magic damage at point-blank. Don't facecheck for a Hookshot before your E is reliable; eat a Slingshot or a Q pull with no escape up and a poke trade becomes a fight you lose.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are a clean skill phase — the blobs he sheds on ability use heal back anything you poke, so don't burn HP unless you can step on them after to deny the pickup. Start W for the outer-edge max-HP damage and self-heal, and respect Stretching Strikes: it is an attack reset as well as a 14s pull, so the wind-up is the tell. Unstable Matter nukes you at point-blank every 5s. Don't facecheck for a wall angle before Hookshot is up — eat a 21s Elastic Slingshot with no escape and the poke trade becomes a fight you lose.

At 6 your R is the answer to a bouncy tank — pull him into the arena away from his team and his loose blobs so he can't Slingshot out or onto a carry, then re-cast Q for the true-damage hit and W%-HP him down. Keep E held to dodge his Q pull and Slingshot, then re-stun once they're on cooldown.
edits.after: This is your window. From Level 3 your W outer blade chunks his max HP and heals you off him faster than his blobs refill, so win short trades and stamp every blob he drops. At 6 The Hextech Ultimatum answers a bouncy tank — but it anchors him where he stands and brings YOU to him, so choose the ground before you press it, then Q-recast for true damage and W him down. Hold E for Stretching Strikes' 14s and a 21s Elastic Slingshot, then re-engage.

edits.before: Zac reclaims the late game — that's the honest read on a 51.55% lane that's barely yours on paper. Once he hits two items he's an unkillable engage tank: his passive revives him from a surviving blob, and your W%-HP and Q true damage stop being enough to delete him before he blobs back up and Slingshots your carries. Your job is to have cashed in your Level 3-to-first-item lead — crack his tower, take plates, and roam — because in a 5v5 his engage and front-line value beat your single-target burst. Don't chase the solo kill into his team; split-push and let your damage dealers handle the blob.
edits.after: Zac reclaims the late game — that's the honest read on a 51.55% lane that's barely yours on paper. Once he hits two items he is an engage tank: Cell Division revives him from a surviving blob, and your W max-HP damage and Q true damage stop being enough to delete him before he blobs back up and Slingshots your carries. The revive runs on its own five-minute timer, though, so a Zac who has already spent it is killable for a long stretch. Cash in your Level 3-to-first-item lead — crack his tower, take plates, and roam — because in a 5v5 his engage beats your single-target burst. Split-push and let your damage dealers handle the blob.

notes: The important fix is that Camille's ultimate was described twice as dragging Zac away from his team. Riot's text is 'Camille dashes to target champion, anchoring them to the area' — she travels to him and pins him where he already is. The already-audited mirror states this correctly from Zac's side ('her R does not move you — she comes to you'), so the two directions were contradicting each other and this page was giving advice that puts Camille inside Zac's team rather than outside it. Both now agree, and the practical instruction is inverted accordingly: choose the ground before pressing R. Also reused the mirror's five-minute figure for the Cell Division revive, which turns his 'unkillable' late game into a state with a window.
